newsitem.title: BULGARIA: POLICE STOP BUS SMUGGLING CHILDREN TO TURKEY.
newsitem.headline: POLICE STOP BUS SMUGGLING CHILDREN TO TURKEY.

text.p: Police said on Wednesday they had found 12 Bulgarian children hidden in a tourist coach travelling to Turkey in the biggest case of human smuggling for 20 years.
The children, from Bulgaria's ethnic Turkish minority, had been expected to join relatives in Turkey. The smugglers were due to receive 1,000 German marks per child, the police said in a statement.
The children, whose age ranged from four to 12, were discovered early on Monday as the bus tried to cross into Turkey at the Malko Turnovo border check-point.
The children had been concealed in two specially prepared places on the bus, which belonged to the Turkish-Bulgarian firm Unur'95, and were in some danger for their life, police said.
Police declined to specify what danger this might be but the children probably could not breathe freely.
Four of the children were accompanied by their father and mother, who were arrested along with the driver of the bus and a Turkish citizen.

Some 800,000 ethnic Turks live in Bulgaria. Many more have emigrated to Turkey in the past decade, culminating in a mass exodus in 1989 to escape a campaign by then communist dictator Todor Zhivkov to force them to adopt Slavic Bulgarian names.
Some ethnic Turks still try to enter Turkey illegally to rejoin relatives or to seek better economic conditions. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 4145
